title: torch backend: keras.utils.split_dataset requires tensorflow
body: The `keras.utils.split_dataset` function requires tensorflow to be installed even tho the docstring states that the `dataset` argument can be a `torch.utils.data.Dataset` (and I assumed that means it would just work on the torch dataset with no issues).

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Same pytorch user just here.
Keras 3 will use tf as backend as default if `KERAS_BACKEND` is not set.
You can export ENV variable or just add this at the top of your python script:
```
import os
os.environ["KERAS_BACKEND"] = "torch"
```

I think this will helps?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Thanks but that isn't the issue. I've set the `KERAS_BACKEND` environment variable to `torch` I can fit and evaluate and evaluate my pytorch model with pytorch dataloaders just fine, but spliting my pytorch dataset with `keras.utils.split_dataset` fails because I don't have tensorflow installed.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hi @reporter - 

The error `ImportError: This requires the tensorflow module. You can install it via 'pip install tensorflow' `occurs because [split_dataset](https://keras.io/api/utils/python_utils/#splitdataset-function) function is trying to apply tensorflow-specific operations like `tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices` and after splitting,  it returns a tuple of two [tf.data.Dataset](https://<redacted-host>/api_docs/python/tf/data/Dataset) objects even if you are using `torch.utils.data.Dataset`. To resolve this error, you can either install tensorflow or use Pytorch's [random_split ](https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/data.html#torch.utils.data.random_split)function. Thanks!
